clue.text: Bats desire birds to leave lake

parts.note: will is wish or desire

indicators.note: to leave means the lake's letter departs from the birds, taken out of them

parts.note: owls are birds
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Bats, keen for the birds to clear off the lake, have their roost to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' suggests the flying mammals, which fits the birds and lake; it is the cricket kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are traditionally made of willow wood, so the material stands for the bat.

clue.text: Stitch up with nurse in classy area

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the stitch word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to sew is to stitch
to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: Framing someone with the help of a nurse in a posh district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' reads as frame, but 'up' reverses SEW. The West End is London's fashionable theatre and shopping district.
explanation.definitionFit: The West End of London, and of many cities, is the affluent, fashionable quarter.

clue.text: Only redeveloped southern city

indicators.note: redeveloped means the letters are rebuilt in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Only a southern city has been regenerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyons is the traditional English spelling of Lyon, a major French city.

clue.text: Playful animal despicable sort beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the word for despicable sort

parts.note: a rotter is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A frisky animal, a real scoundrel, meets an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Otters are famously playful river mammals, often seen sliding and frolicking.

clue.text: Pain accordingly doubled?

definitions.meaning: accordingly means so, and two of them joined by and makes the phrase

explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome person is called a pain or a so-and-so, a euphemism for something ruder.

clue.text: Leader, one from France entering race

indicators.note: entering means the French number goes inside the word for race

parts.note: a tribe is a race or people
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A French leader enters a race, perhaps an election contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a tribune was an elected official championing the people, hence a popular leader.

clue.text: Immature creature bit person from Krakow?

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
Krakow is in Poland, so its native is a Pole

explanation.surface: A young animal nibbled a man from Krakow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larva of a frog or toad, an immature creature.

clue.text: Able to resist crackers?

parts.note: suggests a snack biscuit refused, but crackers are code-breakers: a puzzle they cannot solve resists them

explanation.definitionFit: An unsolvable problem cannot be cracked, so it holds out against anyone trying.

clue.text: Going straight again — and let out with gun!

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, scrambled

explanation.surface: A reformed criminal, released with a gun, hardly going straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' reads as released from prison, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal on AND LET and GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untangled has been straightened out again, its knots removed.

clue.text: Discharge policeman found in south-western river

indicators.note: found in means the policeman sits inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
plod is British slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A policeman discharged after being found in a Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode is to discharge violently, as a gun or bomb does.

clue.text: Pint-sized worker creates writing system

parts.note: pint-sized means small or short
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A small employee invents a new script.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is an abbreviated script of symbols used for rapid note-taking, such as Pitman.

clue.text: Arrangement to have TV in higher place

parts.note: a TV set
up means located higher

explanation.surface: An arrangement for mounting the television high on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is the way things are organised or laid out, a configuration.

clue.text: Certain result to invest Republican — and Democrat!

definitions.note: used as a past participle, 'made certain'

indicators.note: to invest here means to surround, so the verb for result encloses the party letter

parts.note: to ensue is to result or follow

explanation.surface: A result is guaranteed if both US parties put money in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain' is read as a verb in the past, made certain; 'to invest' means to besiege, so R sits inside ENSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have guaranteed an outcome is to have made it certain, so the verb in its past form fits.

clue.text: Soldiers disembark round Floridian city

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
to land is to come ashore
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Troops come ashore near a city in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a large city in central Florida, home of Walt Disney World.

clue.text: Doctor coped with some rot

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor managed a patient with some decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram signal on COPED and SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To decay is to break down organically, which is what rotting matter does.

clue.text: Agreement to involve government statisticians in count

indicators.note: to involve means to include, so the count takes in the statisticians

parts.note: a census is an official count of people
ONS is the UK Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: An agreement to bring official statisticians into the population count.
explanation.walkthrough: The ONS is the UK government body that runs the census.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general agreement reached by a group.

clue.text: Lead astray?

parts.note: suggests tempting someone into sin, but read as ruling a country badly

explanation.definitionFit: To rule poorly is to lead a nation the wrong way, taking 'lead' as govern.

clue.text: Call taken by English beauty

indicators.note: taken by means the call word is followed and collected by the English letter

parts.note: to bell, or give someone a bell, is to telephone them

explanation.surface: An English beauty answers a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired one at a gathering.

clue.text: Enthusiast returning lives in capital

indicators.note: returning means the word for enthusiast is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic or fan
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A fan comes back to live in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: Feline in tattered coat gives touching display

indicators.note: in places the feline inside the rearranged coat
tattered means the coat is torn up, its letters rearranged

parts.note: a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cat in a ragged coat makes a moving show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' suggests emotional, but the piece is named from the Italian for touched; 'tattered' gives TOCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece showing off the player's touch and dexterity.

clue.text: Revolting animals were so stubborn?

definitions.meaning: in Orwell's Animal Farm the rebelling beasts were led by pigs, so they were headed by pigs

explanation.definitionFit: Being obstinately set in one's ways is likened to the reputedly stubborn pig.

clue.text: Mine — one almost complete — becomes inadequate

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: almost means the word for complete loses its last letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A mine nearly finished turns out a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful can mean contemptibly poor or woefully insufficient.

clue.text: Left in strong wind aboard ship

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
on means aboard

explanation.surface: Someone left aboard a ship in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Annihilate French from the besieged city

parts.note: des is French for 'from the' or 'of the'
Troy was besieged by the Greeks for ten years

explanation.surface: The French wipe out a city under siege.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to wipe out completely, the same as annihilating.

clue.text: One to smoke in bed — it takes brave person to intervene!

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the brave person goes inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a hero is a brave person

explanation.surface: Smoking in bed is risky; it takes someone brave to step in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar cut square at both ends, something to smoke.

clue.text: Child tucking into pork pies not the smallest, for example

indicators.note: tucking into means the child is put inside the slang word

parts.note: pork pies is rhyming slang for lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child eating pork pies, not the smallest ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for lies; 'tucking into' looks like eating but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, as 'not the smallest' means quite large.

clue.text: Grand invested in bank for dynamic sort

indicators.note: invested in means the grand goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds put into a bank by a go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' and 'bank' suggest finance, but bank is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a fierce, energetic person, as in an economic tiger.

clue.text: Taken from Sanskrit it lends book name

indicators.note: taken from means the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A book's name borrowed from Sanskrit.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's name is its title.

clue.text: Path is covered in beer

indicators.note: covered in means the word is is enclosed by the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A walkway is swimming in spilt beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage or path between rows of seats or shelves.

clue.text: Warplane circling about cargo ship

indicators.note: circling means the warplane surrounds the word for about

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A military jet circles over a cargo vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a vessel carrying goods, a cargo ship.

clue.text: Stadium accommodating second large team

indicators.note: accommodating means the stadium holds the letter for second inside it

parts.note: an arena is a stadium

explanation.surface: A stadium houses the second-largest team.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a north London football club, a team in the Premier League.

clue.text: Creche in North Surrey moved

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A day-care centre in north Surrey has relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a day-care centre for young children, as is a nursery.
